clue.text: Good boy feeling pleasure

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A well-behaved youngster is happy about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling pleasure is pleased or happy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Arch-villains disposing of property and laying up treasure

indicators.note: getting rid of something, so the property's letters are removed from the villains

parts.note: taken as written before the removal
a villa is a piece of property, a house

indicators.note: in a down clue, laying something up turns it to read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pet is a treasure, a cherished darling

explanation.surface: Master criminals selling off real estate while stashing loot away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch-villains' reads as one hyphenated word but splits after 'Arch', the definition. 'disposing of' signals the removal and 'laying up' turns the treasure upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of the foot is the part also called the instep.

clue.text: Certain people crash Tim's stag do

indicators.note: to crash a party is to gatecrash, but here it signals the letters being wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Some guests gatecrash Tim's stag party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' looks like gatecrashing; it rearranges TIMSSTAGDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatists are people utterly sure of their opinions, so they are certain in a humorous sense.

clue.text: Nun, scratching head, pegs out smalls

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
to peg out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A nun hangs out her small laundry on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pegs out smalls' suggests a washing line, but 'pegs out' means dies. Smalls is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, smalls are underclothes, the same items more casually named here.

clue.text: Debris of party in riotous rag week

indicators.note: the party letter sits inside the rearranged letters
wild and disorderly, signalling the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, a political party

explanation.surface: The mess left after a party during a wild student rag week.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag week is a British student charity week of stunts. 'riotous' rearranges RAGWEEK, and C goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is the scattered remains of something destroyed, a synonym for debris.

clue.text: Report unfortunate discharge

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: poor means unfortunate, as in the poor fellow

explanation.surface: An account of an unhappy release, perhaps from a factory or hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a liquid is to let it flow out, which is what pouring does.

clue.text: Oh! It's time to go!

parts.note: the letters O and H stand for zero and hour, so the word written out in full gives the two-word phrase

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm that it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: O is a zero and H the abbreviation for hour, so 'Oh' is what this phrase shortens to.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the moment an operation is scheduled to begin, the time to set off.

clue.text: Meet one's maker, while wearing pyjamas inside out

indicators.note: the outer letters wear the inner word like clothing, holding it inside
the inside is taken out of the word, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: as means while, as in as I was leaving

explanation.surface: Dying while dressed in pyjamas put on wrong side out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' seems to describe badly worn nightwear, but it means emptying the word of its inside letters; 'wearing' then puts the shell around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass, or pass away, is a euphemism for dying, as is meeting one's maker.

clue.text: Prince Charles, perhaps, starts to lecture architects — numbingly dispiriting experience

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words, their opening letters, are taken

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: Prince Charles giving architects one of his famously deadening lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles (now King Charles III) famously attacked modern architecture, and owns large estates such as the Duchy of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles holds vast estates, so he is an example of someone who owns land.

clue.text: Watch last in series

definitions.meaning: the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of anything

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the final episode of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet ends on this letter, and it is also a famous watchmaker's name.

clue.text: Workers occupying barricade, showing modicum of intelligence

indicators.note: the workers sit inside the barricade as occupiers of it

parts.note: a dam is a barrier, blocking water
TU is short for trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: Strikers occupying a barricade show a little sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' suggests brains, but here it means information.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single item of information, and intelligence can mean information gathered.

clue.text: Get into debt, asking no questions

parts.note: to incur something, like a debt, is to get into it
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Running up debts without enquiring about the terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who asks no questions lacks curiosity, which is what the word describes.

clue.text: Arachne's misconduct upset force

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, so 'Arachne's' means the setter is, I'm

indicators.note: conducting the letters badly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The setter admits that bad behaviour upset the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'misconduct' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force behind movement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: About to receive a broadcast (see below)

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the phrase is taken by sound

parts.note: you're 'in for a' treat means you are about to receive one

explanation.surface: Soon to receive a programme, with a cross-reference pointing lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means below, used in texts as 'vide infra', see lower down.

clue.text: Boris sheds clothes on foolish date, as we may deduce

indicators.note: one piece placed on, following, the other

parts.note: April 1st, April Fools' Day, written APR I

indicators.note: taking off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson stripping off on a silly date, as one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: BORIS stripped of its ends gives ORI, after APR I.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from first principles to conclusions, which is deduction.

clue.text: Spaniard eats expensive and tasteless stuff in Wittering

indicators.note: the name swallows the other piece, taking it inside

parts.note: Ramon is a Spanish man's name
bling is flashy, showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A Spaniard eating some overpriced junk in a village called Wittering.
explanation.walkthrough: Wittering is also an English village, but here it is the verb: to witter is to talk at length about trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: To witter, a British word, is to talk at length about trivial things, a synonym for talking aimlessly.

clue.text: Sibs enjoy pinching playfellow

indicators.note: the words pinch, or steal, the letters held between them

explanation.surface: Brothers and sisters like nipping a friend they play with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playfellow' looks like a playmate, but means a fellow who writes plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist wrote plays, so he is a fellow of the theatre.

clue.text: Waller walls up 100 11s

indicators.note: the name encloses the number like a wall built round it

parts.note: Fats Waller, the American jazz pianist
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A builder walls in a hundred items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waller' looks like someone building a wall; it is the jazz pianist Fats Waller. The answer to 11 across is an item of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of information are things known to be true, synonyms of the plural of 11 across.

clue.text: Meet criminal grass at side of road

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a verge is the grassy strip beside a road

explanation.surface: Meeting a crook informer by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' suggests an informer; here it is real grass on a verge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge come together, meeting at one point.

clue.text: Tip: every second counts during stroke

indicators.note: taking every second letter, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Advice to a rower or swimmer: each second matters in the stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as advice but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a foot or shoe is its toe, so a tip in that sense.

clue.text: Food for tramp in Spooner's mantraps

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: a mantrap catches men: male tricks
a mantrap catches men: male tricks

explanation.surface: Something for a vagrant hidden in mantraps, the Reverend Spooner warns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' suggests a vagrant; here it is a hike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers carry this mix of nuts and dried fruit to eat on the trail, food for a long tramp.

clue.text: Indicates position of red giant using sound waves

indicators.note: something carried by sound waves is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Karl Marx, a giant of communism, the Reds

explanation.surface: Sonar locating a red giant star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red giant' suggests a kind of star; it is Karl Marx, red meaning communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark where something is is to show its location, indicating its place.

clue.text: One seaman treated for memory loss

indicators.note: worked on, processed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor being given medical care for forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' looks medical; it rearranges ISEAMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for loss of memory, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fellow afloat almost two thirds of mile inside Italian city

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: Milan is a city in Italy
a kilometre is about 0.62 miles, almost two thirds of a mile

explanation.surface: A boatman in an Italian city some way from a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thirds of mile' suggests taking MI; instead a km is just under two thirds of a mile. A milk float is a British electric milk-delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: The man who delivers milk drives a milk float, so he is jokingly a fellow afloat.

clue.text: Home Secretary has support of Sun? We're in trouble

parts.note: Theresa May was Britain's Home Secretary when the puzzle appeared
in a down clue, DAY sits beneath SUN to make Sunday, supporting it

explanation.surface: A minister backed by a tabloid paper, the Sun, signals a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here 'Sun' becomes Sunday when DAY is placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The international distress call means we need help urgently.

clue.text: I amend rough average

indicators.note: rough or crude, signalling the letters are roughed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone correcting a rough calculation of the mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle value of a set is one kind of average in statistics.

clue.text: The Budweiser Corporation?

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, and Budweiser is a lager, so this is a drinker's paunch, not a brewing company

explanation.surface: A query about the brewing company that makes Budweiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut gained by heavy drinking is a lager-built corporation, slang for a large stomach.

clue.text: When you skip over, bust bounces up and down

indicators.note: to skip something is to leave it out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: boobs is slang for a bust
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: When skipping, a bosom bounces about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip over' looks like jumping; 'skip' drops O, cricket's over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move quickly up and down, as a cork on water does.

clue.text: Crosby Beach imported numerous Gormleys (nether regions to be ignored)

indicators.note: the lower parts of each word are dropped, leaving only their tops, the first letters

explanation.surface: Crosby Beach near Liverpool took in Antony Gormley's many iron figures, their lower halves buried.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby Beach holds Antony Gormley's 'Another Place', a hundred iron men sinking into the sand; 'Crosby' is also the singer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The crooner Bing Crosby is known by this first name, so the surname clues it.

clue.text: "Taxi Driver" — wooden-headed eccentric in New York

indicators.note: the eccentric piece sits inside the city's letters

parts.note: odd means eccentric

explanation.surface: Taxi Driver, the film, with a dim crank in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Taxi Driver suggests the Scorsese film, set in New York; it is Enid Blyton's Noddy, a wooden toy who drives a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid Blyton's wooden toy character drives a little taxi in Toyland.

clue.text: Wanting new long period of global revolution

indicators.note: lacking, so the letter is missing

parts.note: to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: Longing for a new era of worldwide uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising; here it is the Earth's orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is the time the Earth takes to orbit the sun once.

clue.text: Ban organisation after petition started

indicators.note: the organisation comes after the petition

parts.note: to beg is to petition
Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the UN

explanation.surface: A prohibition campaign launched after a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ban' is not a prohibition but Ban Ki-moon, then head of the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has started has begun, the past participle of begin.

clue.text: I'm grateful after a traveller returned love

indicators.note: the thanks comes after the rest
turned back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a Romani is a member of a travelling people
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Thanks given after a wanderer came back to his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A ROMANI into INAMORA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart, so a love.
